model.title: Radial orthogonality does not imply dual 1-conformal flatness
model.seo_title: Radial orthogonality and dual 1-conformal flatness | Alec Kriebel
model.meta_description: An explicit statistical geometry counterexample: every radial orthogonal distribution is integrable, while the dual is nowhere locally 1-conformally flat.
model.abstract: We give a negative answer to Kurose's Question 3(e) in the 1998 collection Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics. For the product S²(1) × ℝ with its product metric and Levi–Civita connection, every radial orthogonal distribution in that question is integrable, but the dual statistical structure is nowhere locally 1-conformally flat. Integrability follows from the first variation of energy; nonflatness follows from two curvature evaluations. A conformal metric and projective connection change also give an example with nowhere zero cubic tensor. The same obstruction works in every dimension at least three. The proof is independent of computation. Historical priority is unresolved; no claim of a first resolution is made.

model.native_description_html:
We give an explicit negative answer to Takashi Kurose's Question 3(e) in Furuhata, Matsuzoe and Urakawa, Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics (1998), p.126, indexed as AMR-059-0011 / 6000011. On the product S^2(1) x R with its product metric and Levi-Civita connection, every radial orthogonal distribution in the question is integrable, but the dual statistical structure is nowhere locally 1-conformally flat. The proof combines the first variation of energy with two incompatible curvature evaluations. A conformal metric and projective connection deformation yields a non-self-dual example with nowhere zero cubic tensor; the product obstruction extends to every dimension at least three.

The package contains a four-page manuscript, LaTeX source, a standard-library exact rational verifier, an independently implemented SymPy verifier, source and priority audits, and reproducibility instructions. The computations supplement the analytic proof. Historical priority remains unresolved. The documented, bounded search found no earlier explicit answer, but relevant sources remain uninspected, including Kurose's 1999 affine-realization paper, Binder-Simon's 2000 problem list, and the full content of Kurose's 2016 talk. An earlier answer or implicit resolution in those sources cannot be excluded. No first-resolution claim or assertion that the question remained open at publication is made. The ingredients are classical; the exact deformation is credited to Matsuzoe (1999), p.178, equation (2.1).

This is an unrefereed, AI-assisted preprint. The candidate was supplied as AI-generated work. The manuscript, verification materials, and separate adversarial AI audits were prepared with OpenAI Codex. AI reviews are not external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.

scientific_scope.base_family: S²(1) × ℝ^(n−2) with product metric and its Levi–Civita connection, every integer n≥3
scientific_scope.radial_domain: Every center p and every admitted geodesically convex neighborhood U; field defined on U excluding p using the unique affine connecting geodesic terminal tangent line
scientific_scope.base_conclusion: All such radial orthogonal distributions are integrable, while the dual equals the original connection and is nowhere locally statistical 1-conformally flat
scientific_scope.zero_cubic_distinction: Base is self-dual with ∇h=0; additional deformation on S²(1) × ℝ is non-self-dual and has nowhere-zero cubic tensor
scientific_scope.deformation: h₁=eᵗh₀; ∇¹_XY=∇⁰_XY+dt(X)Y+dt(Y)X; same unparametrized connecting geodesics and orthogonality, so same radial fields
scientific_scope.deformed_dual_obstruction: (∇¹)*_XY=∇⁰_XY−h₀(X,Y)∂t; arbitrary further statistical 1-conformal potential ψ yields ∇⁰_XY−h₀(X,Y)grad_h₀(t+ψ), excluded by base obstruction
scientific_scope.flattening_definition: ĥ=e^φh and ∇̂_XY=∇_XY−h(X,Y)grad_hφ; flatness concerns statistical connection, distinct from ordinary conformal flatness of metric
scientific_scope.proof: First variation gives Dᵖ=ker dEₚ; flatness would require R(X,Y)Z=h(Y,Z)A(X)−h(X,Z)A(Y); sphere and mixed-plane evaluations force A(e₁)=e₁ and A(e₁)=0 at every point

model.title: A designed tree model with a sharp congestion–fragmentation transition
model.seo_title: Designed-tree congestion and fragmentation transition | Alec Kriebel
model.meta_description: A designed binary tree links a drop in marginal admitted demand with fragmentation of spare capacity, uniformly over every optimizer outside a shrinking window.
model.abstract: We construct a bounded-degree physical tree model in which the normalized marginal admitted demand drops from one to zero while the spare-capacity graph changes from the entire tree to isolated vertices. Capacities arise from the unique cheapest fixed-topology enlargement supporting doubled initial traffic. Each of the k² cross-root streams has an independent, fixed-law exponential growth rate. An all-cuts estimate confines both changes, with probability tending to one, to an interval of width 16√(log k/k) around mean doubled demand. Both outer-phase conclusions hold for every optimizer. This is a specialized existence response to Aldous's conceptual congestion toy-model request. The width is an upper bound; no critical profile or universal traffic law is asserted.

scientific_scope.physical_model: Complete rooted binary tree height H>=2, k=2^(H-1) leaves on each root side, N=4k-1 vertices, degree<=3; unique paths, fixed topology, k² cross-root streams of initial size one
scientific_scope.design: Strictly positive linear increment prices uniquely force C_e=2kk_e; terminal capacity2k and root-edge capacity2k² grow with k; each designed finite network stays fixed
scientific_scope.growth: Independent Exp(1) slopes X_ij sampled once; d_ij(t)=1+(t-1)X_ij for t>=1; stream mean t and variance(t-1)²; S_k=sum X_ij>0 almost surely
scientific_scope.observables: F_k maximum admitted total; normalized marginal r_k=F'_(k,+)/S_k; spare graph contains all original vertices and exactly strictly slack physical edges, can depend on optimizer inside window
scientific_scope.joint_probability: For every binary k with delta_k=8sqrt(log k/k)<1, with probability at least1-epsilon_k, epsilon_k=2k^-31+2k^-2/(1-k^-2)^2+(4/k²)^k, both outer statements hold simultaneously for every indicated time and every optimizer
scientific_scope.lower_phase: All1<=t<=2-delta_k: all demand admitted, r_k=1, whole physical tree spare, largest component N
scientific_scope.upper_phase: Allt>=2+delta_k: F_k=2k², r_k=0, every edge saturated, spare graph edgeless on original vertices, largest component1
scientific_scope.limits: Fixed1<=t<2: r_k and M_k/N converge in probability to1; fixedt>2 both to0; for any measurable optimizer selection; fixedt>=1 including2: F_k/k² -> min(t,2); outer events eventually almost surely along binary k under any common coupling
scientific_scope.window: Width16sqrt(log k/k) sufficient upper bound; no exact critical scale, matching lower bound, r_k(2) limit or critical component profile
